The Profile Likelihood Returned by statmod_profile()

Source: R/profile_class.R
StatmodProfile.Rd

The object that statmod_profile() returns.

Usage

StatmodProfile(
  points = NULL,
  profiled_labels = character(0),
  profiled_quantities = list(),
  profile_column = character(0),
  unrestricted_point = NULL,
  profile_method = profile_method(),
  hyper_handling = character(0),
  outer_method = NULL,
  is_likelihood_ratio = logical(0),
  joint = logical(0)
)

Arguments

points

The data frame of the points.

profiled_labels

The labels of which.

profiled_quantities

A list of profiled_quantity objects, one for each label.

profile_column

The name of the column of points that is the profile of each label, "outer_criterion" or "profile_pen_loglik", a character vector named by the labels.

unrestricted_point

The data frame of the unrestricted fit.

profile_method

The profile_method object.

hyper_handling

"held" or "refit", the argument hyper of statmod_profile().

outer_method

The outer criterion object of the fit, or NULL.

is_likelihood_ratio

Whether the profile of each label gives a likelihood ratio statistic, so that confint() inverts it, a logical vector named by the labels.

joint

Whether the labels were held jointly.

Value

A StatmodProfile object.

Details

With joint = TRUE the table points has one column for each label, named by the label, and one row for each combination of values held. With joint = FALSE each label is profiled by itself, with the other labels free, and points has the columns profiled_label, the label held in the row, and value, its value. The columns that follow are, in both cases, profile_loglik, profile_penalty, profile_pen_loglik, outer_criterion and converged, described at statmod_profile(). unrestricted_point has the same columns at the fit itself, with one row for each label when joint = FALSE.

See also

statmod_profile(), confint.StatmodProfile(), autoplot.StatmodProfile().

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(60))
dd$y <- 1 + 2 * dd$x + rnorm(60, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
prof <- statmod_profile(fit, which = "mu:x",
                        values = profile_range(width = 2, n = 9))
prof@profile_column
#>                 mu:x 
#> "profile_pen_loglik" 
head(as.data.frame(prof), n = 3)
#>       mu:x profile_loglik profile_penalty profile_pen_loglik outer_criterion
#> 1 1.615742      -23.56354               0          -23.56354       -25.70965
#> 2 1.700842      -22.70458               0          -22.70458       -24.86501
#> 3 1.785942      -22.07563               0          -22.07563       -24.24654
#>   converged
#> 1      TRUE
#> 2      TRUE
#> 3      TRUE
